o: Haggai reproves the Jews for neglecting the temple.
He promises God's assistance to them.
bg: Consists of two brief, comprehensive chapters. The object of the prophet was generally to urge the people to proceed with the rebuilding of the temple.

The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word "son;" the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel. He is also known by the Persian name of Sheshbazzar (Ezra 1:8, 11).
(asked of God), father of Zerubbabel. (Ezra 3:2,8; 5:2; Nehemiah 12:1; Haggai 1:1,12,14; 2:2,23) (B.C. about 580.)
ch.s: This chapter covers: Haggai reproves the Jews for neglecting the temple (vv. 1–11); He promises God's assistance to them (vv. 12–15). People named: Haggai, Zerubbabel, Shealtiel, Joshua, Darius. Places: Judah.
ch.mh: Observe the sin of the Jews, after their return from captivity in Babylon.
q: Read verses 1–11 (Haggai reproves the Jews for neglecting the temple). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 12–15 (He promises God's assistance to them), what do you learn about family and generations?
Verse 6 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Haggai 1:9. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Haggai’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of prophecy and fulfillment in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Haggai?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Those who have lost time, need to redeem time; and the longer we have loitered in folly, the more haste we should make.
ch.a: Memorize the key verse and come back to it each morning this week.

o: Greater glory promised to the second temple than to the first.
bg: Consists of two brief, comprehensive chapters. The object of the prophet was generally to urge the people to proceed with the rebuilding of the temple.

The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word "son;" the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel. He is also known by the Persian name of Sheshbazzar (Ezra 1:8, 11).
(asked of God), father of Zerubbabel. (Ezra 3:2,8; 5:2; Nehemiah 12:1; Haggai 1:1,12,14; 2:2,23) (B.C. about 580.)
ch.s: This chapter covers: Greater glory promised to the second temple than to the first (vv. 1–9); Their sins hindered the work (vv. 10–19); The kingdom of Christ foretold (vv. 20–23). People named: Haggai, Zerubbabel, Shealtiel, Joshua, Darius. Places: Judah, Egypt, No.
ch.mh: Those who are hearty in the Lord's service shall receive encouragement to proceed.
q: Read verses 1–9 (Greater glory promised to the second temple than to the first). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 10–19 (Their sins hindered the work), what do you learn about holiness?
Verse 7 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Malachi 3:1. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Haggai’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of prophecy and fulfillment in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Haggai?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: When we begin to make conscience of duty to God, we may expect his blessing; and whoso is wise will understand the loving-kindness of the Lord.
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.
